decisions.subject: external genesis authority and independently witnessed establishment
decisions.recommended_option: use an already verifiable owner external identity plus a distinct auditor if such evidence exists; otherwise use an in-person dual-control genesis ceremony with a hash-bound signed receipt; never let the new root authorize its own establishment
decisions.compatibility_effect: genesis identity mechanism, attestation bytes/hash, witnesses, review, and transaction ID become root provenance
decisions.supersession_rule: any identity, witness, attestation, review, or transaction change requires a new prospective genesis record

decisions.subject: distinct genesis operator, signer custodian, and auditor roles and custody domains
decisions.recommended_option: freeze three distinct named principals and owner-controlled offline primary custody with a separately controlled recovery domain; serialize logical public identifiers only and never a private path
decisions.compatibility_effect: principal IDs, custody-domain IDs, access controls, recovery and destruction policy, and receipts become root identity
decisions.deadline_gate: before controller specialization or key action
decisions.supersession_rule: any role, domain, access, recovery, retention, or destruction change requires prospective review and new evidence

decisions.subject: dedicated offline root-ceremony environment and exact tools
decisions.recommended_option: use a dedicated owner-controlled offline Linux/OpenSSH environment and bind OS, executable, library, version, argv, output-format, and network-unavailable evidence
decisions.compatibility_effect: environment and tool bytes, versions, fixed argv, dependencies, network state, and output format become ceremony identity
decisions.deadline_gate: before any root controller specialization or action
decisions.supersession_rule: any environment, tool, version, dependency, argv, network, or format change requires a new inventory and review

decisions.subject: encrypted root key, secret-input boundary, KDF work, backup, recovery, rotation, and destruction
decisions.recommended_option: require an encrypted Ed25519 root key, uncaptured interactive secret, exact later KDF work input, separately controlled encrypted recovery, and non-secret access/backup/recovery/rotation/destruction receipts
decisions.compatibility_effect: encoding, KDF/work value, secret boundary, access, backup, recovery, rotation, destruction, and receipt hashes become custody identity
decisions.deadline_gate: before controller specialization or key action
decisions.supersession_rule: any protection, secret, KDF, backup, recovery, rotation, or destruction change requires prospective acceptance

decisions.subject: canonical public key, fingerprint, allowed-signers bytes, scope, and export identity
decisions.recommended_option: construct create-exclusive public-key, SHA256 fingerprint, canonical single-entry allowed-signers, receipt, and sidecar artifacts scoped only to principal and namespace cpu-prefetch-q15-authorization
decisions.compatibility_effect: root public bytes/fingerprint, principal, namespace, artifact IDs, paths, canonical trust bytes/hash, and receipt become authorization identity
decisions.deadline_gate: before root acceptance or P4-K-A signing
decisions.supersession_rule: any public key, scope, path, format, canonical bytes, or artifact identity change requires a new root version and review

decisions.subject: append-only root status, activation, rotation, revocation, compromise, and recovery governance
decisions.recommended_option: use an append-only versioned ledger; require distinct reviewed records for activation, rotation, revocation, and recovery; stop every dependent authorization on suspected compromise; never edit or reuse prior root artifacts
decisions.compatibility_effect: root version, status lineage, activation/revocation instants, authority, reviews, and dependent-authorization invalidation become governance identity
decisions.supersession_rule: lifecycle policy changes require a new prospective ADR; append-only prior status and artifacts are retained
